cases.name: unresolved-status-collision
cases.trap: Choose an authoritative definition for completed from contradictory documents without an accepted decision.
cases.prompt: Two documents in the same workflow domain disagree. An engineering runbook says `completed` means execution stopped, including when it failed. A product requirement says `completed` means the requested goal was achieved. No decision resolving the difference exists. Draft a small vocabulary clarification and explain any required decision.
expectations: Distinguishes execution ended from goal achieved with a case where execution ends unsuccessfully.
Marks the collision unresolved, and identifies the decision needed before terms can be accepted.
Keeps current claims traceable to the two source artifacts.
negative_expectations: Must not declare either meaning accepted without a decision.
Must not silently rewrite requirements or change runtime state names.

cases.name: two-account-contexts
cases.trap: Keep domain definitions separate but invent an unsupported one-to-one relationship or shared ID across them.
cases.prompt: The Identity team calls an authenticated principal an `Account`. The Billing team calls an invoice recipient an `Account`. In one documented example, principal P1 manages billing accounts B1 and B2. Later P2 takes over B2, while B2 keeps its invoice history. No source establishes that principal IDs and billing-account IDs are shared. A colleague proposes one company-wide definition of `Account` to remove duplication. Recommend how the teams should maintain a shared vocabulary and describe the boundary between these concepts.
expectations: Identifies Identity and Billing as distinct bounded contexts and distinguishes an authenticated principal from an invoice recipient.
Preserves the documented one-to-many example (P1 manages B1 and B2) and transfer (P2 takes over B2 without changing its invoice history), without treating either as a universal relationship rule.
Describes cross-context association or translation only as supported by the examples, and marks any further relationship or ID assumptions as unresolved until evidenced.
Uses context-specific qualifiers where ambiguity matters rather than enforcing a global meaning.
negative_expectations: Must not merge authenticated principals with invoice recipients or mandate a single global meaning for Account.
Must not assert a one-to-one mapping, shared IDs, or fixed ownership as facts contrary to or unsupported by the examples.
Must not invent additional mapping rules, schemas, or product decisions to fill unknowns.

cases.name: glossary-not-breaking-rename
cases.trap: Treat a preference for a name as permission for an incompatible API and persistence migration.
cases.prompt: A team proposes the domain term `Run` instead of `Job`. Public API clients still send `jobId`, event consumers expect `JobCreated`, and persisted records contain `job_id`. The assignment is to update the glossary only. Draft the vocabulary change and identify follow-up work.
expectations: Records Run as proposed and Job as current/legacy usage, not a fully completed adoption.
Identifies the API, event, persistence, and consumer compatibility boundaries.
Limits the result to the authorized glossary scope; describes a separately reviewed migration if adoption is approved.
negative_expectations: Must not rename externally visible identifiers or persisted fields as a cosmetic cleanup.
Must not state that the new vocabulary is already implemented.

cases.name: go-style-not-domain-semantics
cases.trap: Invoke an unnecessary vocabulary process for a straightforward Go identifier convention.
cases.prompt: A Go developer asks: `Should our struct field be UserID or UserId?` There is no disagreement about what the field means. What guidance is appropriate, and does this need a domain glossary entry?
expectations: Routes to idiomatic Go naming guidance and answers the narrow naming question (UserID).
Explains why no domain-meaning clarification or glossary addition is needed.
negative_expectations: Must not invent different business concepts for ID and Id.
Must not mandate a shared-language workflow for an identifier-style question.

cases.name: accepted-meaning-vs-legacy-code
cases.trap: Mistake code terminology for intended product meaning or prematurely change storage contracts.
cases.prompt: A product owner has explicitly approved this domain distinction: `Booking` is a held reservation before payment; `Order` is a confirmed paid purchase. Existing code sometimes labels both as Order, and the task is only to draft vocabulary. Produce a compact vocabulary entry or discrepancy note.
expectations: Records the approved business distinction with source, context, status and a distinguishing example.
Reports the code's observed legacy usage separately from approved product meaning.
Flags any future renames or data changes as work requiring explicit compatibility analysis and scope.
negative_expectations: Must not infer business intent from inconsistent code labels.
Must not claim the code is already aligned or change persisted fields as part of glossary drafting.

cases.name: missing-vocabulary-with-unresolved-meaning
cases.trap: Leave recurring domain distinctions only in chat, or wait for all terms to be agreed before proposing a durable vocabulary.
cases.prompt: A documentation refactor is authorized for the local backup domain. The repository guide places domain material under docs/domains/<domain>/ and the supplied complete documentation inventory has no vocabulary. Accepted requirements at docs/domains/backup/requirements.md#br-12 and #br-13 distinguish Finished (execution stopped, possibly unsuccessfully) from Succeeded (the requested backup was verified). docs/domains/backup/guide.md and docs/domains/backup/architecture.md repeatedly call both outcomes Done. Draft docs/domains/backup/cancellation-design.md uses Cancelled for a stop request; draft docs/domains/backup/cancellation-product-note.md uses it for execution actually stopping. No accepted decision settles that word. Describe the concrete documentation edits and supply the resulting small vocabulary content, with its location and source links. Do not claim to have changed files in this text-only task.
expectations: Places a small durable backup vocabulary under the supplied repository structure and links the affected user and architecture documentation to it instead of leaving the result only as a discrepancy report.
Preserves Finished and Succeeded as accepted meanings sourced to BR-12 and BR-13, including an unsuccessful terminal execution that distinguishes them.
Records the conflicting Cancelled meanings and their draft sources as unresolved, with the decision still needed; creation does not wait for agreement on that term.
Limits edits to the authorized documentation scope and describes proposed edits rather than claiming actual file writes.
negative_expectations: Must not adopt one Cancelled meaning as accepted or introduce a new runtime state.
Must not replace the project structure with a required global glossary location.
Must not conflate execution stopping with verified backup success.

cases.name: reuse-embedded-domain-vocabulary
cases.trap: Create a competing dictionary because the existing vocabulary is embedded in a domain overview rather than a file named glossary.md.
cases.prompt: The repository index links docs/reservations/overview.md#terms as the maintained reservation vocabulary. Its accepted definitions say Hold is a temporary reservation before payment and Booking is a confirmed paid reservation, sourced to decision D-7. An unrelated Finance glossary defines Booking as an accounting entry. An authorized edit to docs/reservations/guide.md uses 'booking' for an unpaid Hold. There is no glossary.md file. Describe the smallest correction and any vocabulary edits or links needed. Use only these facts; the request does not authorize changing Finance or product behavior.
expectations: Reuses the Terms section in docs/reservations/overview.md as the reservation vocabulary and preserves its accepted definitions and D-7 provenance.
Corrects the unpaid reservation usage to Hold in the affected guide and links to the existing Terms section without creating a second dictionary.
Keeps the Finance meaning in its separate context and does not merge the two meanings of Booking.
negative_expectations: Must not create a competing glossary merely because no glossary.md file exists.
Must not move or rewrite the maintained definitions just to match an example path.
Must not alter Finance terminology or introduce new reservation behavior.

cases.name: review-only-missing-vocabulary
cases.trap: Treat a conditional glossary-creation rule as authorization to write during a review-only assignment.
cases.prompt: Review only: do not edit repository files. A check of the repository index and the affected workflow documents found no vocabulary. The user guide calls every stopped run 'successful'; accepted requirement BR-9 reserves Successful for a confirmed outcome and permits unsuccessful stopped runs. This confusion recurs in two design notes. Produce the review finding and recommend a concrete follow-up. The repository guide places workflow domain notes in docs/workflows/.
expectations: Reports the consequential mismatch with BR-9, the guide and design notes, and an example of a stopped run with an unconfirmed outcome.
Recommends a small vocabulary at a suitable location under docs/workflows/ and related document corrections as follow-up, without claiming a file was created.
Keeps review completion separate from resolution of the underlying terminology mismatch.
negative_expectations: Must not claim repository edits, resolution or implemented alignment from the review report alone.
Must not weaken BR-9 to match the guide or expand the task into runtime changes.

cases.name: unresolved-meaning-survives-handoff
cases.trap: Turn a proposed glossary term or a forwarded concern into an accepted decision when the next agent lacks the earlier conversation.
cases.prompt: Prepare a standalone handoff for another agent to continue authorized documentation work. docs/workflows/vocabulary.md records Completed as unresolved: draft docs/workflows/design.md uses execution ended, while draft docs/workflows/product-note.md uses goal achieved. Neither definition has been accepted. Concern F-17 records this collision; its decision owner is unknown. A failed execution distinguishes the meanings. An unrelated correction to Retry wording in docs/workflows/guide.md was checked against accepted BR-4. API clients still consume status='completed', and API changes are outside this assignment. The next agent can read repository files and the handoff, but cannot access your chat or concern system. Write the handoff.
expectations: Carries both Completed meanings, their exact source paths, unresolved status, the failed-execution counterexample and the decision still needed into the accessible handoff.
Keeps ownership unknown and records F-17 as a source identity while including the essential evidence that cannot be retrieved from the concern system.
Distinguishes the verified BR-4 Retry wording correction from the unresolved Completed decision and out-of-scope API compatibility work.
Points the recipient to the existing vocabulary and requires affected documents or consumers to be checked before claiming alignment.
negative_expectations: Must not promote a draft definition to accepted, invent a decision owner, or treat F-17 as resolved because it was forwarded.
Must not require the previous chat or an inaccessible concern link to understand the conflict.
Must not authorize an API rename or report existing clients migrated.
